Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. The information set forth in Item 1.02 of this Current Report on Form 8-K is incorporated herein by reference. Item 1.02 Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement. As previously disclosed, on December 10, 2025, Enova International, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into the Agreement and Plan of Merger, as amended on December 18, 2025 (as amended, the “Merger Agreement”), by and between the Company and Grasshopper Bancorp, Inc. (“Grasshopper”), a Delaware corporation and the parent holding company of Grasshopper Bank N.A. (“Grasshopper Bank”), a national bank and wholly-owned subsidiary of Grasshopper, pursuant to which, and subject to the terms and conditions therein, (i) Grasshopper was to merge with and into the Company (the “Merger”), and (ii) immediately following the Merger, an interim national bank and wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company was to merge with and into Grasshopper Bank. On October 16, 2026, the Company and Grasshopper entered into the Mutual Termination Agreement and Release (the “Termination Agreement”) pursuant to which the parties agreed to mutually terminate the Merger Agreement effective as of such date. Under the terms of the Termination Agreement, the Company made a $4,000,000 cash payment to Grasshopper. Neither party will pay any other fees or have any other liabilities to each other related to the Merger Agreement. The foregoing summary of the Merger Agreement and the Termination Agreement is not complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the complete text of the Merger Agreement, which is contained in Annex A to the proxy statement/prospectus included in the Registration Statement on Form S-4 (File No. 333-292287) filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on December 19, 2025, and amended on December 29, 2025, and the complete text of the Termination Agreement, which is attached as Exhibit 10.1 hereto and is incorporated herein by reference. Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers On October 13, 2026, Titan International, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into a deferred compensation arrangement (the "Plan") with Paul G. Reitz, the Company’s President and Chief Executive Officer, whereby the Company awarded Mr. Reitz deferred compensation in the amount of $2.3 million, subject to the vesting and payment terms of the Plan (the "Deferred Compensation Amount"). Payment of the Deferred Compensation Amount will not commence until 2030 and will thereafter be made in a lump sum or installments, as elected by Mr. Reitz in accordance with the terms of the Plan. The Plan and Trust Agreement were approved by the Compensation Committee of the Company's Board of Directors (the "Committee") and the Company's Board of Directors on October 12, 2026. In connection with the Plan, the Company has established an irrevocable rabbi trust (the "Trust") pursuant to the terms of a trust agreement dated October 13, 2026 (the "Trust Agreement"). Pursuant to the Trust Agreement, the Company will contribute to the Trust approximately 332,370 shares of the Company’s common stock (the "Shares") having a value of approximately $2.3 million based on the average of the high and low trading prices of the Company's common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on October 13, 2026, to assist the Company in funding its obligations under the Plan. The Company has agreed to make additional contributions to the Trust from time to time as required under the Plan. The assets held in the Trust remain subject to the claims of the Company’s general creditors in the event of the Company’s insolvency. Mr. Reitz does not have a preferred claim on, or beneficial ownership interest in, the assets of the Trust, and his rights under the Plan and Trust Agreement are unsecured contractual rights against the Company. The Trustee will make payments to Mr. Reitz and his beneficiaries in accordance with the applicable payment provisions of the Plan and Trust Agreement, although the Company may elect to pay benefits due under the Plan directly rather than through the Trust. To the extent the Trust assets are insufficient to satisfy amounts due under the Plan, the Company remains obligated to pay the balance. All rights associated with Trust assets, including voting rights with respect to the shares of the Company’s common stock held by the Trust, will be exercised by the Trustee and may not be exercised by Mr. Reitz. The Trust will terminate when Mr. Reitz and his beneficiaries are no longer entitled to benefits under the Plan, at which time any remaining assets will revert to the Company. Amounts payable to Mr. Reitz will be determined in accordance with the terms of the Plan, and payments from the Trust will be made in accordance with the applicable payment schedule under the Plan. The foregoing descriptions of the Plan and Trust Agreement do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the applicable agreements, copies of which are filed as exhibits to this Current Report on Form 8-K and incorporated herein by reference.
